input.rationale: Both limbs of the assignment bargain sit at or beyond our walk-away line. Section (c) ASSIGNMENT (p0149) imposes a one-way, blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment with no Affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, while leaving Licensor free to assign (including to our competitors). Article XX(a) (p0134) then makes any Change of Control of Licensee — including a sale of substantially all assets or a merger (p0135) — an automatic termination of the Agreement and all of our licenses unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever the acquirer is competitive with it or it merely "believes" its interests are adversely affected. That is precisely the vendor change-of-control exit the playbook prohibits. Our redline makes the assignment right mutual with an Affiliate/successor carve-out, bars Licensor assignment to a Licensee competitor, applies a not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments, and converts Article XX(a) from a Licensor termination/consent trigger into a notice obligation while preserving the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition relied on elsewhere. Fallback if pressed: mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent not unreasonably withheld for other transfers.

(a) Simultaneously with the execution hereof, the Licensor shall issue to the Licensee 350,000 shares of its common stock as a bonus.

The amount of rebates earned by Licensee shall be calculated for each tranche of 30 Billion of Notional Volume traded in the EPath FX Platform by Licensee. Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

During the period commencing on the Acceptance Date through the thirty six (36th) month anniversary of this Agreement, the Licensor shall remit to Licensee a series of rebates based upon the amount of Notional Volumes traded on the EPath FX Trading Platform by Licensee. The computation of the rebates received by Licensee shall be expressed as a fixed percentage (15%) of Billable Platform Fees paid by Licensee to Licensor. The rebates shall be payable in shares of Licensor's Common Stock; priced at $.25 cents per share. The amount of rebates earned by Licensee shall be calculated for each tranche of 30 Billion of Notional Volume traded in the EPath FX Platform by Licensee. The amount of shares earned by Licensee shall terminate at the earlier of, the expiration of the term of this Agreement or the receipt of Six (6,000,000) Million shares of Licensor's common stock by Licensee. By way of illustration, if the Licensee trades 30 Billion of Notional Volume on the Platform, with a Billable Platform Fee of $279,000. The rebate to Licensee will be calculated as follows: Rebate = 15% of $279,000 = $41,850; Shares of Licensor representing $41,850/$.25 = 167,400 shares of Licensor."},{"id":"p0077","text":"V. system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor. Upon any breach by Licensee of any representation, warranty, covenant and/or obligation hereunder, the Licensor may immediately terminate this Agreement and prohibit the Licensee's use of any and/or all of the Licensed Technology.
input.rationale: The Agreement locks Licensee into a 36-month Initial Period (renewable for seven years at Licensor's option) with no right for Licensee to terminate for convenience anywhere in the document. The only termination triggers run in Licensor's favour (breach under Article IV and Article II, insolvency under Article XIX, Change of Control and wind-up under Article XX), and Article XXI/XXIII confirm Licensor retains all rights and payment entitlements on exit. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under T4C (missing behaviour). Licensor has no convenience right on short notice, so only the Customer-side gap needs fixing. We added a 30-day Licensee convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination charge or acceleration of Supplemental Payments, and express confirmation that Licensor may not terminate for convenience during the term.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

During the period commencing on the Acceptance Date through the thirty six (36th) month anniversary of this Agreement, the Licensor shall remit to Licensee a series of rebates based upon the amount of Notional Volumes traded on the EPath FX Trading Platform by Licensee. The computation of the rebates received by Licensee shall be expressed as a fixed percentage (15%) of Billable Platform Fees paid by Licensee to Licensor. The rebates shall be payable in shares of Licensor's Common Stock; priced at $.25 cents per share. The amount of rebates earned by Licensee shall be calculated for each tranche of 30 Billion of Notional Volume traded in the EPath FX Platform by Licensee. The amount of shares earned by Licensee shall terminate at the earlier of, the expiration of the term of this Agreement or the receipt of Six (6,000,000) Million shares of Licensor's common stock by Licensee. content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — ASSIGN**

The agreement fails the rule on both limbs:

1. **§(c) ASSIGNMENT (p0149)** — one-way, blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment or transfer without Licensor's consent, with no Affiliate or merger/asset-sale carve-out, no reasonableness standard, and no reciprocal restriction on Licensor (so Licensor could assign to our competitor).
2. **Article XX(a) (p0134)** — our Change of Control (defined at p0135 to include a sale of substantially all assets or a merger) **automatically terminates the Agreement and all our licenses** unless Licensor consents, and Licensor is deemed reasonable in refusing whenever the acquirer competes with it or it merely believes its interests are affected. This is the walk-away scenario in the playbook.

**Redline validated (ok:true):** mutual assignment right with an Affiliate/successor carve-out, a bar on Licensor assigning to a Licensee competitor, a not-unreasonably-withheld standard for other assignments, confirmation that a Change of Control is not a deemed assignment, and conversion of Article XX(a) into a post-closing notice obligation (the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition is preserved for other cross-references). Fallback noted in the comment: mutual assignment to successors on written notice.

Related point left unredlined as outside this rule: Article XXII gives Licensor a right of first refusal over our M&A transactions — worth flagging separately if it is in scope for another rule.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Both limbs of the assignment bargain sit at or beyond our walk-away line. Section (c) ASSIGNMENT (p0149) imposes a one-way, blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment with no Affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, while leaving Licensor free to assign (including to our competitors). Article XX(a) (p0134) then makes any Change of Control of Licensee — including a sale of substantially all assets or a merger (p0135) — an automatic termination of the Agreement and all of our licenses unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever the acquirer is competitive with it or it merely "believes" its interests are adversely affected. That is precisely the vendor change-of-control exit the playbook prohibits. Our redline makes the assignment right mutual with an Affiliate/successor carve-out, bars Licensor assignment to a Licensee competitor, applies a not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments, and converts Article XX(a) from a Licensor termination/consent trigger into a notice obligation while preserving the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition relied on elsewhere. Fallback if pressed: mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent not unreasonably withheld for other transfers.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Planner hints:

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

**Finding submitted: `missing` (T4C — Termination for convenience), confidence 0.86**

**What I found**

- **Article IV (p0049)** sets a **36-month Initial Period**, renewable for a further **seven years at Licensor's sole option**, and contains no Licensee exit right.
- Searching the whole agreement, every termination trigger runs **in Licensor's favour**: breach (Art. II p0043 and Art. IV p0049), insolvency (Art. XIX p0132, mutual but not convenience), Change of Control (Art. XX p0134), and wind-up (p0137).
- **Article XXI (p0138)** and **Article XXIII (p0142)** reinforce that on any termination Licensor retains all rights, including payment entitlements — so exit is costly and one-sided.
- There is **no Licensor termination-for-convenience right**, so the walk-away trigger on that limb is not engaged; the gap is purely on our side.

**Why this is a deviation**

Under T4C, the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (missing behaviour). Here the commitment is 36 months plus a unilateral seven-year renewal option, with volume-based fees, $2,500/month support and 33% Supplemental Payments continuing throughout.

**Redline proposed (validated `ok:true`)** — new Article IV.IV inserted after p0049:

> Termination for Convenience. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Licensee may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, without penalty, early termination charge, or acceleration of any user fees, Supplemental Payments or other amounts. Upon such termination, Licensor shall refund to Licensee any prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective date of termination... Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any renewal or extension term.

The drafting deliberately blocks **acceleration of Supplemental Payments** on exit (the planner's flagged risk) and reaches the preferred position with a single insertion rather than restructuring Article IV. The negotiation comment offers the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a three-month fee cap) if Licensor pushes back.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement locks Licensee into a 36-month Initial Period (renewable for seven years at Licensor's option) with no right for Licensee to terminate for convenience anywhere in the document. The only termination triggers run in Licensor's favour (breach under Article IV and Article II, insolvency under Article XIX, Change of Control and wind-up under Article XX), and Article XXI/XXIII confirm Licensor retains all rights and payment entitlements on exit. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under T4C (missing behaviour). Licensor has no convenience right on short notice, so only the Customer-side gap needs fixing. We added a 30-day Licensee convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination charge or acceleration of Supplemental Payments, and express confirmation that Licensor may not terminate for convenience during the term.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Licensor hereby, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement, grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
input.rationale: The grant in p0030 runs to Licensee alone, and the restrictions confine access to "the employees of the Licensee" (p0045), bar third-party use or sublicensing without consent (p0041, p0042, p0085) and bar assignment without Licensor's consent (p0149) — so our Affiliates and contractors are excluded with no path to add them. In addition, Article IV (p0049) lets Licensor immediately terminate the licence upon "any breach" of any covenant with no materiality threshold or cure period, which makes the licence effectively revocable at Licensor's discretion. Our redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (subject to Field of Use and confidentiality), permits assignment to a successor in an M&A transaction, and limits Licensor's revocation right to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice.

proposal.summary: Extend licence grant to Licensee's Affiliates and contractors, permit assignment to a successor, and limit revocation to uncured material breach
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the grant to cover our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and to permit transfer to a successor in a merger or sale, since our licences must be usable across our group and survive corporate reorganisations. We have also conditioned Licensor's termination right on a material breach that remains uncured after notice, so the licence is not effectively revocable at will; as a fallback we can accept Affiliate coverage on written notice to Licensor.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

input.rationale: The grant in p0030 runs to Licensee alone, and the restrictions confine access to "the employees of the Licensee" (p0045), bar third-party use or sublicensing without consent (p0041, p0042, p0085) and bar assignment without Licensor's consent (p0149) — so our Affiliates and contractors are excluded with no path to add them. In addition, Article IV (p0049) lets Licensor immediately terminate the licence upon "any breach" of any covenant with no materiality threshold or cure period, which makes the licence effectively revocable at Licensor's discretion. Our redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (subject to Field of Use and confidentiality), permits assignment to a successor in an M&A transaction, and limits Licensor's revocation right to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice.

proposal.summary: Extend licence grant to Licensee's Affiliates and contractors, permit assignment to a successor, and limit revocation to uncured material breach
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the grant to cover our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and to permit transfer to a successor in a merger or sale, since our licences must be usable across our group and survive corporate reorganisations. We have also conditioned Licensor's termination right on a material breach that remains uncured after notice, so the licence is not effectively revocable at will; as a fallback we can accept Affiliate coverage on written notice to Licensor.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
input.rationale: Article III vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and its IP in Licensor, and "DERIVATIVE WORK" (1.3) is defined to capture any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based on the Licensed Technology. Combined with Article VII(b), under which we pay Licensor for further development and customization work including a unique client front end, the drafting means we own nothing we pay to have developed and receive only the narrow, terminable, Field-of-Use licence in Article II. There is also no provision anywhere reserving our rights in our own trading, order, client and account data or configurations, and Article I's "Intellectual Property Rights" and "Confidential Information" definitions run only in Licensor's favour. That falls short of the playbook position that we own deliverables created for us and retain all rights in our data, with Licensor keeping its pre-existing platform IP subject to a licence back. The redline adds a narrow carve-out to Article III (Licensee Data ownership, assignment of paid-for customization deliverables with a perpetual royalty-free licence back of embedded Licensor IP, and no joint ownership) without disturbing Licensor's ownership of the Platform.

proposal.summary: Carve Licensee Data and paid-for customization deliverables out of Licensor's blanket ownership in Article III, with a licence-back of embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article III gives Licensor ownership of all Licensed Technology and Derivative Works (defined to include additions, improvements and enhancements), which would sweep in our trading and client data and the custom front end we pay Licensor to build under Article VII(b); our position is that we own our data and what we pay to have developed, while Licensor keeps its platform IP. We have therefore added an ownership carve-out with a licence back of any embedded Licensor IP, and would accept as a fallback Licensor ownership of the customization deliverables plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for us to use, modify and sublicense them for our business.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing: (a) Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data and content submitted, generated or transmitted by or on behalf of Licensee through the Licensed Technology, including its trading, order, client and account data and its records, reports and configurations (collectively, "Licensee Data"), Licensor acquires no right, title or interest in Licensee Data, and Licensor shall use Licensee Data solely to perform its obligations under this Agreement; (b) all customization work, deliverables and work product developed by Licensor specifically for Licensee and paid for by Licensee (including any unique client front end developed under Article VII(b)) shall be owned by Licensee, and Licensor hereby assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest therein, provided that Licensor retains ownership of its pre-existing Licensed Technology and Intellectual Property Rights and hereby grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any such pre-existing materials to the extent embedded in or reasonably necessary to use such deliverables; and (c) nothing in this Agreement creates or shall be construed to create joint ownership of any Intellectual Property Rights.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

**Finding: deviation (high) — Licence grant scope**

The grant (p0030) runs only to Licensee, and the surrounding restrictions actively lock out our group: access is limited to "employees of the Licensee" (p0045), third-party use and sublicensing require Licensor consent (p0041, p0042, p0085), and assignment is blocked without consent (p0149). Article IV (p0049) also permits immediate termination of the licence on *any* breach, with no materiality threshold or cure period — close to the walk-away position of a licence revocable at Licensor's discretion.

Redline submitted (validated, preferred level):
- **p0030** — grant extended to "its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Licensee's behalf," with an override making such use permitted without further consent (subject to Field of Use and confidentiality), plus a right to assign to a successor by merger, consolidation, reorganisation or sale of substantially all assets/equity.
- **p0049** — termination narrowed to a *material* breach that remains uncured 30 days after written notice, removing "immediately."

Fallback noted in the comment: Affiliate coverage on written notice to Licensor, with successor transfer preserved.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The grant in p0030 runs to Licensee alone, and the restrictions confine access to "the employees of the Licensee" (p0045), bar third-party use or sublicensing without consent (p0041, p0042, p0085) and bar assignment without Licensor's consent (p0149) — so our Affiliates and contractors are excluded with no path to add them. In addition, Article IV (p0049) lets Licensor immediately terminate the licence upon "any breach" of any covenant with no materiality threshold or cure period, which makes the licence effectively revocable at Licensor's discretion. Our redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (subject to Field of Use and confidentiality), permits assignment to a successor in an M&A transaction, and limits Licensor's revocation right to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

input.quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV(b) binds Licensee (our party) to permit Licensor-initiated audits of its records with no cap on frequency, no advance notice period (the 30 days is a deadline for us to submit to the audit, not notice to us), no business-hours or minimal-interference limit, no confidentiality undertaking from the auditor, and no restriction confining access to accounting records rather than our systems. Unlimited, on-demand audits sit at the playbook walk-away line. Cost allocation is already compliant (p0064: Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy exceeding 5% is found), and auditor independence/mutual selection is acceptable, so the minimal edit adds only the frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality and no-system-access limits to the second sentence of p0073.

During the period commencing on the Acceptance Date through the thirty six (36th) month anniversary of this Agreement, the Licensor shall remit to Licensee a series of rebates based upon the amount of Notional Volumes traded on the EPath FX Trading Platform by Licensee. The computation of the rebates received by Licensee shall be expressed as a fixed percentage (15%) of Billable Platform Fees paid by Licensee to Licensor. The rebates shall be payable in shares of Licensor's Common Stock; priced at $.25 cents per share. The amount of rebates earned by Licensee shall be calculated for each tranche of 30 Billion of Notional Volume traded in the EPath FX Platform by Licensee. The amount of shares earned by Licensee shall terminate at the earlier of, the expiration of the term of this Agreement or the receipt of Six (6,000,000) Million shares of Licensor's common stock by Licensee. By way of illustration, if the Licensee trades 30 Billion of Notional Volume on the Platform, with a Billable Platform Fee of $279,000. The rebate to Licensee will be calculated as follows: Rebate = 15% of $279,000 = $41,850; Shares of Licensor representing $41,850/$.25 = 167,400 shares of Licensor."},{"id":"p0077","text":"V. paragraphs.text: GENERAL PROVISIONS

(a) GOVERNING LAW. The parties agree that it is to their mutual benefit that their respective rights and obligations under this Agreement are guided by, and their disputes hereunder are determined in accordance with, a well developed body of law. Accordingly, the parties agree that the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A., applicable to contracts entered in and performed entirely within the State of New York, U.S.A. without regard to any conflict of law principles.

The parties agree that any legal suit, action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement must be instituted in the City of New York, State of New York, and the parties each (i) irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, or any court of the State of New York, and (ii) waives any objection to the venue of any such suit, action or proceeding and any claim relating to forum non conveniens.

In any such suit, action, or proceeding, any summons, order to show cause, writ, judgment, decree or other process may be delivered to the parties outside the State of New York or outside the United States and when so delivered, such party shall be subject to the jurisdiction of such court, and amenable to the process so delivered as though the same had been served within the State of New York but outside the county in which such suit, action or proceeding is pending.

(b) COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS. Licensee agrees to comply in all material respects with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its activities under this Agreement, including without limitation, any applicable export controls imposed by the U.S. Export Administration Act of 1978, as amended (the "ACT") and the regulations promulgated under the Act.

(c) ASSIGNMENT. Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent. Any attempt to assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner Licensee's license rights hereunder without such consent will be void and of no effect. For purposes of this Agreement, any Change of Control (as defined in Section 13.4(a)) shall be governed by the provisions of the section entitled Change Of Control and not the provisions of this Section Subject to the terms of this Section, this Agreement will bind and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

(d) ATTORNEYS' FEES. In the event that any action or proceeding is brought in connection with this Agreement, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its costs and reasonable attorneys' fees following a final judgment.

(e) SEVERABILITY. If for any reason a court of competent jurisdiction finds any provision of this Agreement invalid or unenforceable, then that provision of the Agreement will not be voided, but rather will be enforced to the maximum extent legally permissible and the other provisions of this Agreement will remain in full force and effect.

(f) INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR. The parties to this Agreement are independent contractors and this Agreement will not establish any relationship of partnership, joint venture, employment, franchise, or agency between the parties. Neither party will have the power to bind the other or incur obligations on the other's behalf without the other's prior written consent.

(g) NOTICES. All notices required or permitted under this Agreement will be in writing and delivered by confirmed facsimile transmission, by courier or overnight delivery service, or by certified mail, and in each instance will be deemed given upon receipt. All communications to a party will be sent to the address of the party set forth in the preamble above or to such other address as may be specified by such party to the other in accordance with the Section called Contact Information. Either party may change its address for notices under this Agreement by giving written notice to the other party by the means specified in this Section.
(h) COUNTERPARTS. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which will be deemed an original, but both of which together will constitute one and the same instrument.

(e) ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement, constitutes the complete and exclusive agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding and replacing any and all prior and contemporaneous agreements, communications, and understandings (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter.

(h) MODIFICATION. No modification to this Agreement, nor any waiver of any rights, shall be effective unless consented to in writing and the waiver of any breach or default shall not constitute a waiver of any other right or of any subsequent breach or default.

(i) FORCE MAJEURE. Except for the obligations to make payments hereunder, each Party shall be relieved of the obligations hereunder to the extent that performance is delayed or prevented by any cause beyond its reasonable control, including without limitation, acts of God, public enemies, war, civil disorder, fire, flood, explosion, labor disputes or strikes or any acts or orders of any governmental authority.
(j) CONSTRUCTION. The parties agree that no ambiguity (if any) found in this Agreement shall be resolved against any party by virtue of its participation in the drafting of this Agreement.

(k) REPRESENTATION BY COUNSEL. Each party acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to be represented by separate independent counsel in the negotiation of this Agreement, that any such respective attorneys were of its own choosing, that each authorized representative has read this Agreement and that it understands its meaning and legal consequences to each party. Each Party warrants and represents that it has consulted with its attorney of choice, or voluntarily chose not to do so, concerning the execution, the meaning and the import of this Agreement, and has read this Agreement and fully understands the terms hereof as signified by its signature below, and is executing the same of its own free will for the purposes and consideration herein expressed. Each Party warrants and represents that it has had sufficient time to consider whether to enter into this Agreement and that it is relying solely on its own judgment and the advice of its own counsel, if any, in deciding to execute this Agreement. Each Party warrants and represents that it has read this Agreement in its entirety and has consulted with its attorney, if any concerning the execution of this Agreement. If any or all Parties have chosen not to seek counsel, said party or parties hereby acknowledge that it or they refrained from seeking counsel entirely of its or their own volition and with full knowledge of the consequences of such a decision.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed as of the Effective Date by their duly authorized representatives.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding submitted — deviation (critical, ip-data).**

**What the document does:** Article III (p0048) vests *all* right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and its Intellectual Property Rights in Licensor. Because "DERIVATIVE WORK" (§1.3, p0005) is defined as any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based on the Licensed Technology, and Article VII(b) (p0087) contemplates that we pay Licensor for "further development and customization work for creating a unique client front end," we would fund bespoke development and own none of it — receiving only the narrow, terminable Field-of-Use licence in Article II (p0030, p0043). There is also no provision anywhere reserving our rights in our own trading, order, client and account data; the "Confidential Information" and "Intellectual Property Rights" definitions run one way, in Licensor's favour only.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** a single inserted paragraph after Article III that (a) confirms we retain all rights in Licensee Data and that Licensor may use it only to perform the Agreement, (b) assigns to us the customization deliverables we pay for, with Licensor keeping its pre-existing platform IP and granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to any of that IP embedded in the deliverables, and (c) rules out joint ownership. Licensor's ownership of the Platform itself is untouched, which is acceptable under the playbook.

**Fallback offered in the comment:** Licensor may own the customization deliverables provided we get a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them for our business.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Article III vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and its IP in Licensor, and "DERIVATIVE WORK" (1.3) is defined to capture any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based on the Licensed Technology. Combined with Article VII(b), under which we pay Licensor for further development and customization work including a unique client front end, the drafting means we own nothing we pay to have developed and receive only the narrow, terminable, Field-of-Use licence in Article II. There is also no provision anywhere reserving our rights in our own trading, order, client and account data or configurations, and Article I's "Intellectual Property Rights" and "Confidential Information" definitions run only in Licensor's favour. That falls short of the playbook position that we own deliverables created for us and retain all rights in our data, with Licensor keeping its pre-existing platform IP subject to a licence back. The redline adds a narrow carve-out to Article III (Licensee Data ownership, assignment of paid-for customization deliverables with a perpetual royalty-free licence back of embedded Licensor IP, and no joint ownership) without disturbing Licensor's ownership of the Platform.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (medium severity) — Article IV(b), ¶p0073**

**What the document says.** The only audit right binding us is Article IV(b): Licensee must allow an independent CPA or Audit Professional (mutually selected) to audit accounting records, with the audit "permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor."

**Why it deviates.**
- **Frequency:** no cap at all — Licensor could audit repeatedly. This approaches the walk-away position (unlimited audits).
- **Notice:** the "30 days" is a deadline for *us to submit*, not advance notice to us — effectively an on-demand audit.
- **No business-hours / minimal-interference limit**, no confidentiality undertaking from the auditor, and nothing confining review to accounting records rather than our systems.

**Already acceptable (left untouched):**
- Cost allocation at ¶p0064 — Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy exceeding 5% is found — matches the preferred position exactly.
- Auditor independence and mutual selection.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Replaced only the second sentence of ¶p0073 to add: once per twelve months; 30 days' prior written notice; normal business hours with no unreasonable interference; auditor confidentiality undertaking; access limited to relevant accounting records (which we may provide off-site or electronically), with no direct or remote access to our systems, networks or data.

**Negotiation posture.** The comment flags that we can drop to 15 days' notice if 30 is impractical; the 5% cost trigger already sits at our preferred level, so there is no need to trade there.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Article IV(b) binds Licensee (our party) to permit Licensor-initiated audits of its records with no cap on frequency, no advance notice period (the 30 days is a deadline for us to submit to the audit, not notice to us), no business-hours or minimal-interference limit, no confidentiality undertaking from the auditor, and no restriction confining access to accounting records rather than our systems. Unlimited, on-demand audits sit at the playbook walk-away line. Cost allocation is already compliant (p0064: Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy exceeding 5% is found), and auditor independence/mutual selection is acceptable, so the minimal edit adds only the frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality and no-system-access limits to the second sentence of p0073.

No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: Article III vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and its IP in Licensor, the broad 'Derivative Work' definition (1.3) sweeps in additions/enhancements, and Article VII(b) contemplates Licensee paying for customization (including a unique client front end) with no ownership or assignment to Licensee and no reservation of Licensee data rights — squarely short of the IP rule's preferred position.

Redline is directionally correct and minimal: it leaves Licensor's ownership of its pre-existing Platform/Licensed Technology intact and adds a 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' carve-out that (i) reserves Licensee ownership of its trading, order, client and account data, (ii) assigns paid-for customization deliverables to Licensee with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back of embedded Licensor IP, and (iii) disclaims joint ownership — covering all three limbs of the redline guidance.
No assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Licensor remains, so the walk-away trigger is cleared; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies cleanly.

Comment is accurate to the cited text (Article III, 1.3, Article VII(b)), uses the required prefix and first-person-plural professional tone, explains the change and cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (Licensor ownership plus perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).
Ancillary addition that Licensor may use Licensee Data only to perform its obligations is a proportionate corollary of the data-ownership reservation and does not constitute material scope creep.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.
