Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: In the event of such immediate termination Licensor shall retain all of it rights under this Agreement and applicable law including but not limited to the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology.
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, stipulated penalty, shortfall charge, minimum-volume commitment or early-termination fee is payable by us as Licensee. The fee provisions (p0050-p0074, p0086) are purely usage-based per-trade fees plus a $2,500/month support fee, with no minimum spend or acceleration on termination. On termination for our breach the Licensor only "retain[s] ... the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology" (p0049), i.e. accrued fees actually earned, not a stipulated sum. Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return/certification obligations and no exit payment, and Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages against either party. The only cost-shift is the audit-cost provision (p0064) triggered by a >5% discrepancy, which is a reimbursement of actual audit cost rather than a penalty. Nothing to redline under this rule; note that Article XIII (p0130) caps only the Licensor's liability, which is addressed by the liability-cap rule rather than here.

During the period commencing on the Acceptance Date through the thirty six (36th) month anniversary of this Agreement, the Licensor shall remit to Licensee a series of rebates based upon the amount of Notional Volumes traded on the EPath FX Trading Platform by Licensee. The computation of the rebates received by Licensee shall be expressed as a fixed percentage (15%) of Billable Platform Fees paid by Licensee to Licensor. The rebates shall be payable in shares of Licensor's Common Stock; priced at $.25 cents per share. The amount of rebates earned by Licensee shall be calculated for each tranche of 30 Billion of Notional Volume traded in the EPath FX Platform by Licensee. The amount of shares earned by Licensee shall terminate at the earlier of, the expiration of the term of this Agreement or the receipt of Six (6,000,000) Million shares of Licensor's common stock by Licensee. By way of illustration, if the Licensee trades 30 Billion of Notional Volume on the Platform, with a Billable Platform Fee of $279,000. The rebate to Licensee will be calculated as follows: Rebate = 15% of $279,000 = $41,850; Shares of Licensor representing $41,850/$.25 = 167,400 shares of Licensor."},{"id":"p0077","text":"V. input.quote: In the event of such immediate termination Licensor shall retain all of it rights under this Agreement and applicable law including but not limited to the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology.
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, stipulated penalty, shortfall charge, minimum-volume commitment or early-termination fee is payable by us as Licensee. The fee provisions (p0050-p0074, p0086) are purely usage-based per-trade fees plus a $2,500/month support fee, with no minimum spend or acceleration on termination. On termination for our breach the Licensor only "retain[s] ... the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology" (p0049), i.e. accrued fees actually earned, not a stipulated sum. Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return/certification obligations and no exit payment, and Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages against either party. The only cost-shift is the audit-cost provision (p0064) triggered by a >5% discrepancy, which is a reimbursement of actual audit cost rather than a penalty. Nothing to redline under this rule; note that Article XIII (p0130) caps only the Licensor's liability, which is addressed by the liability-cap rule rather than here.

Licensor shall provide certificates of insurance to Licensee on request.

input.rationale: Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS", all warranties "WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED" are disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant that nonconformity to the Documentation "CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED." There is no affirmative performance or conformity warranty anywhere in the Agreement (the only other "warrants" references are Licensee-side or boilerplate representations at p0159). You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

I reviewed the fee and payment mechanics (Article V and the volume-band tiers, p0050–p0074), the Supplemental Payments and support-fee provisions (p0077–p0089), the term/termination and post-termination articles (p0049, p0132–p0142), and General Provisions (p0145–p0159), and searched for "liquidated damages," "penalty," "minimum," and "shall pay."

Key points:
- **No Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.** All Licensee payments are usage-based per-trade fees plus a fixed $2,500/month support charge; there is no minimum-volume commitment, shortfall charge, late-payment interest or acceleration.
- **No early-termination fee.** On termination for our breach, Licensor only retains the right to receive payments "for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology" (p0049) — accrued fees, not a stipulated sum. Article XXI (p0138) requires only return of materials and an officer's certificate.
- **Article XXIII (p0142)** affirmatively bars termination damages against either party, which supports our position.
- The audit cost-shift on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is reimbursement of actual audit cost, not a penalty, so it does not trigger this rule.

One adjacent observation flagged for the liability-cap rule rather than this one: Article XIII (p0130) caps only the Licensor's liability (at one half of amounts paid) and leaves our indemnity in Article XII (p0128) uncapped.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No liquidated damages, stipulated penalty, shortfall charge, minimum-volume commitment or early-termination fee is payable by us as Licensee. The fee provisions (p0050-p0074, p0086) are purely usage-based per-trade fees plus a $2,500/month support fee, with no minimum spend or acceleration on termination. On termination for our breach the Licensor only "retain[s] ... the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology" (p0049), i.e. accrued fees actually earned, not a stipulated sum. Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return/certification obligations and no exit payment, and Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages against either party. The only cost-shift is the audit-cost provision (p0064) triggered by a >5% discrepancy, which is a reimbursement of actual audit cost rather than a penalty. Nothing to redline under this rule; note that Article XIII (p0130) caps only the Licensor's liability, which is addressed by the liability-cap rule rather than here.

p0049: ARTICLE IV TERM I Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period"). The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor. Upon any breach by Licensee of any representation, warranty, covenant and/or obligation hereunder, the Licensor may immediately terminate this Agreement and prohibit the Licensee's use of any and/or all of the Licensed Technology. In the event of such immediate termination Licensor shall retain all of it rights under this Agreement and applicable law including but not limited to the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology. ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance

Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration)**

Article VIX contains no affirmative warranty at all — only an "AS IS" disclaimer that expressly sweeps in **express** warranties and states that Licensor does not warrant that nonconformity to the Documentation "CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED." That is the playbook walk-away position, so we redlined it:

1. **Inserted new § 9.1 (Limited Warranty)** — workmanlike performance of any services/support/implementation work; 12-month conformity of the Licensed Software to its Documentation; compliance with applicable laws; no malicious code — with a repair / replace / re-perform / refund remedy at Licensor's option.
2. **Narrowed the disclaimer** (p0110) with an "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THE LIMITED WARRANTY ABOVE" lead-in so the express warranty is not swallowed by the "express or implied" disclaimer.

Fallback flagged in the comment: 90-day conformity period with the same remedies.

Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS", all warranties "WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED" are disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant that nonconformity to the Documentation "CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED." There is no affirmative performance or conformity warranty anywhere in the Agreement (the only other "warrants" references are Licensee-side or boilerplate representations at p0159). This sits at the playbook walk-away position. Redline inserts a limited warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformity to Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/refund remedy and carves that express warranty out of the disclaimer so it is not swallowed; fallback is a 90-day conformity period.

Original paragraphs:
p0109: WARRANTY DISCLAIMER
p0110: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
p0111: DISCLAIMS ALL WARRANTIES CONCERNING THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY, WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT
p0115: UNINTERRUPTED,TIMELY SECURE OR ERROR-FREE, OR THAT ERRORS IN THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY OR NONCONFORMITY TO ITS
p0116: DOCUMENTATION CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED.

Resolved definitions:
Licensor: SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT THIS SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT ("Agreement") is made and entered into as of this 27th day of April 2009 by and between SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX, a Delaware Corporation whose principal address is 575 Madison Avenue, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10022 ("Licensor"), and 551 FX IB Associates, LLC a Delaware Limited Liability Company, whose principal address is located at 575 Madison Avenue, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10022 ("Licensee").

LICENSED TECHNOLOGY: 1.9 "LICENSED TECHNOLOGY" means the Licensed Know-How and the Licensed Software, collectively.

Rendered redline:
p0109: WARRANTY DISCLAIMER
LIMITED WARRANTY. Licensor warrants that: (a) any services, support, implementation or training work performed by Licensor under this Agreement will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery, the Licensed Software will conform in all material respects to its Documentation; (c) Licensor will comply with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement; and (d) the Licensed Technology will be delivered free of viruses, worms, time bombs, disabling code and other malicious code. Licensee's remedy for breach of the foregoing warranties is, at Licensor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming services or Licensed Technology, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services or Licensed Technology.
p0110: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THE LIMITED WARRANTY ABOVE, THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY

Comment:
[Playbook] Article VIX currently disclaims all warranties, express and implied, so we have no recourse if the Licensed Technology does not work as documented. We have added a limited warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformity to Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/refund remedy, and carved it out of the disclaimer; we can accept a 90-day conformity period if needed.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: missing (insurance covenant absent) — redline validated and submitted.**

- **Investigation:** The section outline contains no insurance article. Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

The Agreement has no insurance article; the only reference to "insurance" (p0051) is a cost pass-through to Licensee, not a coverage covenant. Inserted a short insurance covenant as new General Provisions subsection (l) after p0159 at the playbook preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback flagged in the comment.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligations after Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return everything on termination but gives us no exit rights, so we have added a reciprocal wind-down provision: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: ARTICLE XXI-A TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing. For purposes of this Article, "Licensee Data" means all data, records and information of Licensee or its customers, including trade, order and transaction records, that is submitted to, hosted, processed or stored by Licensor in connection with this Agreement.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return everything on termination but gives us no exit rights, so we have added a reciprocal wind-down provision: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: ARTICLE XXI-A TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing. For purposes of this Article, "Licensee Data" means all data, records and information of Licensee or its customers, including trade, order and transaction records, that is submitted to, hosted, processed or stored by Licensor in connection with this Agreement.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.rationale: The Agreement has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return provision. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs entirely in Licensor's favour: our licence terminates automatically and we must ship back all Licensed Technology and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, with all Licensor rights surviving. Nothing requires Licensor — which hosts our market data, order and trade records on its platform (Articles II/IV) — to return our data, to provide any wind-down help, or to delete our data afterwards. The confidentiality article (p0124) imposes obligations only on Licensee, and Articles XIX–XXIII contain no exit mechanics. In a hosted trading platform of this kind, absence of these rights is a deviation; we inserted a new Article XXI-A giving six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with a 90-day assistance fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligations after Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return everything on termination but gives us no exit rights, so we have added a reciprocal wind-down provision: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: ARTICLE XXI-A TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing. For purposes of this Article, "Licensee Data" means all data, records and information of Licensee or its customers, including trade, order and transaction records, that is submitted to, hosted, processed or stored by Licensor in connection with this Agreement.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligations after Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return everything on termination but gives us no exit rights, so we have added a reciprocal wind-down provision: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: ARTICLE XXI-A TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing. For purposes of this Article, "Licensee Data" means all data, records and information of Licensee or its customers, including trade, order and transaction records, that is submitted to, hosted, processed or stored by Licensor in connection with this Agreement.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. input.rationale: The Agreement has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return provision. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs entirely in Licensor's favour: our licence terminates automatically and we must ship back all Licensed Technology and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, with all Licensor rights surviving. Nothing requires Licensor — which hosts our market data, order and trade records on its platform (Articles II/IV) — to return our data, to provide any wind-down help, or to delete our data afterwards. The confidentiality article (p0124) imposes obligations only on Licensee, and Articles XIX–XXIII contain no exit mechanics. In a hosted trading platform of this kind, absence of these rights is a deviation; we inserted a new Article XXI-A giving six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with a 90-day assistance fallback offered in the comment.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control
input.rationale: The Agreement has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return provision. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs entirely in Licensor's favour: our licence terminates automatically and we must ship back all Licensed Technology and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, while all Licensor rights survive. Nothing requires Licensor — which hosts our market data, order and trade records on its platform — to return our data, provide wind-down help, or delete our data afterwards. The confidentiality article (p0124) binds only Licensee, and Articles XIX–XXIII contain no exit mechanics. For a hosted trading platform this absence is a deviation; we inserted a new Article XXI-A giving six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with a 90-day fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligations after Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return everything on termination but gives us no exit rights, so we have added a reciprocal wind-down provision: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: ARTICLE XXI-A TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing. For purposes of this Article, "Licensee Data" means all data, records and information of Licensee or its customers, including trade, order and transaction records, that is submitted to, hosted, processed or stored by Licensor in connection with this Agreement.

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligations after Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return everything on termination but gives us no exit rights, so we have added a reciprocal wind-down provision: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: ARTICLE XXI-A TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing. For purposes of this Article, "Licensee Data" means all data, records and information of Licensee or its customers, including trade, order and transaction records, that is submitted to, hosted, processed or stored by Licensor in connection with this Agreement.

input.rationale: The Agreement has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return provision. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs entirely in Licensor's favour: our licence terminates automatically and we must ship back all Licensed Technology and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, with all Licensor rights surviving. Nothing requires Licensor — which hosts our market data, order and trade records on its platform (Articles II/IV) — to return our data, to provide any wind-down help, or to delete our data afterwards. The confidentiality article (p0124) imposes obligations only on Licensee, and Articles XIX–XXIII contain no exit mechanics. In a hosted trading platform of this kind, absence of these rights is a deviation; we inserted a new Article XXI-A giving six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with a 90-day assistance fallback offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

**Finding submitted: `missing` (medium severity) — TRANSITION**

**What I found.** The Agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data-return provision. Article XXI (p0138, "Effect of Termination") is entirely one-directional: our licence terminates automatically, we must ship back all Licensed Technology, API documentation and Confidential Information within five days and have an officer certify compliance, and "[a]ll of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." I also checked the confidentiality article (p0124 — binds Licensee only), the insolvency/change-of-control termination triggers (p0132–p0137), the non-exclusive remedy article (p0142), and searched the full document for data/export/deletion language. Nothing obliges Licensor to return our hosted market data, order and trade records, to help us migrate, or to delete our data afterwards — a material gap in a hosted FX trading platform arrangement.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Inserted a new Article XXI-A after p0138 tracking the playbook's preferred position: (a) up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates on our request; (b) return of Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within 30 days; (c) deletion thereafter with written certification. Because the Agreement has no "Customer Data" equivalent defined term, I defined "Licensee Data" inline to cover our and our customers' trade, order and transaction records hosted or processed by Licensor.

**Negotiation posture.** The comment flags the 90-day fallback (with the same 30-day export) if Licensor resists a six-month assistance window. Note the walk-away risk is live here: with no provision at all, Licensor could take the position it may delete our records immediately on termination, which is problematic given FX trade-record retention expectations.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return provision. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs entirely in Licensor's favour: our licence terminates automatically and we must ship back all Licensed Technology and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, while all Licensor rights survive. Nothing requires Licensor — which hosts our market data, order and trade records on its platform — to return our data, provide wind-down help, or delete our data afterwards. The confidentiality article (p0124) binds only Licensee, and Articles XIX–XXIII contain no exit mechanics. For a hosted trading platform this absence is a deviation; we inserted a new Article XXI-A giving six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with a 90-day fallback offered in the comment.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: ARTICLE VII TECHNICAL SUPPORT SERVICES (a) The Licensor shall provide Technical Support Services relating to the maintenance and support of the Software and the Licensee shall pay the Licensor $2,500 per month for such Technical Support Services.
input.rationale: Platform user fees are purely usage-based (per US$1m traded, Article V and the volume bands), and there is no minimum volume, take-or-pay floor or shortfall penalty on us. However, the $2,500 monthly Technical Support Services fee is mandatory and non-reducible for the entire 36-month Initial Period (p0049), which provides us no termination for convenience. That is a fixed minimum spend of roughly $90,000 with no exit, contrary to the playbook position that fees should be for usage or ordered services only. The minimal fix adds a 30 days' notice right to discontinue or reduce the support services with pro-rated fees and confirms no minimum purchase commitment; the fallback (commitment limited to a 12-month period with a true-up) is offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

**Finding submitted: deviation (medium, commercial) — MINCOMMIT.**

What I found:
- **No classic take-or-pay.** Article V and the volume-band table (p0056–p0063) price the license purely on actual `Monthly Notional Volume` traded; there is no minimum volume, no shortfall charge, and no volume cap on our usage. The "in no event shall the amount payable be less than..." language in p0070 is only a floor equal to actual recorded trades, not a commitment.
- **The Vendor-side commitments** (rebate shares, bonus shares, enhancements at no cost) run in our favour and were not flagged.
- **The problem is Article VII(a) (p0086):** a mandatory, non-reducible $2,500/month support fee that runs for the whole 36-month Initial Period (p0049), which gives us no termination for convenience. That is a de facto ~$90,000 minimum spend with no exit — contrary to the playbook position that fees be for usage or ordered services only.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`): a single in-line addition to p0086 giving us a 30 days' notice right to discontinue or reduce the support services with pro-rated fees, plus a confirmation that we carry no minimum purchase, volume or spend commitment. The comment offers the fallback (commitment capped at a 12-month period with a true-up) if the Licensor resists outright cancellability.

Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — FX Platform License Agreement (Licensor / Licensee)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel for the Customer/Licensee)  
**Re:** Playbook review — 18 verified findings (all verification: pass)

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement is drafted heavily in the Licensor's favour and, as written, contains several terms that sit at or beyond our walk-away lines. Three issues are critical: (i) there is **no Licensor indemnity at all**, while Article XII imposes a broad one-way indemnity on us and Article XIII(a) affirmatively disclaims Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims; (ii) Article III vests **all** IP in the Licensor, including customization work we pay for under Article VII(b), with no reservation of our trading, order, client and account data; and (iii) Article XIII excludes consequential damages and caps liability **only for the Licensor**, at one half of amounts paid — below our six-months'-fees floor — leaving our own liability uncapped and unqualified by any Excluded Claims.

A further cluster of high-severity issues concerns lock-in and exit: a 36-month term with **no Licensee termination for convenience**, a Licensor-only unilateral **seven-year renewal option**, a licence grant that excludes our Affiliates and contractors and is revocable on any breach without cure, and an assignment/change-of-control regime that prohibits our assignment outright while permitting Licensor assignment (including to our competitors) and terminating the Agreement automatically on a Licensee change of control. Medium and low items — audit limits, the fixed support-fee commitment, the 36-month all-personnel non-solicit, absent transition/data-return mechanics, the pure "AS IS" warranty disclaimer, and the absence of any insurance covenant — are addressed by targeted redlines with fallbacks.

Five rules test **compliant** and require no redline: exclusivity, liquidated damages/penalties, non-compete, governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York state and federal courts), and MFN.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / our position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | No Licensor indemnity anywhere; Article XII runs one way against us on very broad triggers, and Article XIII(a) disclaims Licensor liability for IP infringement claims. We add a Licensor defence/indemnity (third-party IP, breach of law, unauthorised access to Licensee data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation and an express carve-out from the Article XIII exclusions and cap, and narrow our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of applicable law. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Article III vests all right, title and interest in Licensor, and the "Derivative Work" definition (1.3) captures improvements; we own nothing we pay to have developed under Article VII(b) and no provision reserves our data. We carve out Licensee Data and paid-for customization deliverables, with a perpetual royalty-free licence back of embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership, leaving Licensor's Platform ownership intact. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Article XIII excludes indirect damages and caps liability for Licensor only, at one half of amounts paid; our liability is uncapped and expanded by Article XII. We make the exclusion and cap mutual, reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, and add Excluded Claims carve-outs (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), confirming fee obligations are not capped damages. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Section (c) bars Licensee assignment outright with no Affiliate/successor carve-out while Licensor may assign freely; Article XX(a) auto-terminates on a Licensee change of control absent Licensor consent, deemed reasonably withheld if the acquirer competes. We make assignment mutual with an Affiliate/successor carve-out, bar Licensor assignment to our competitors, apply a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, and convert Article XX(a) to a notice obligation. Fallback: mutual assignment to successors on notice, consent not unreasonably withheld for other transfers. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | The grant runs to Licensee alone and access is confined to Licensee employees, excluding Affiliates and contractors; Article IV permits immediate termination for "any breach" with no materiality threshold or cure. We extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (subject to Field of Use and confidentiality), permit assignment to an M&A successor, and limit revocation to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice. |
| 6 | High | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Article IV(I) lets Licensor unilaterally extend for a further seven years with no Licensee consent, reminder or pricing cap — and contradicts Article IV(II)–(III), which contemplate extension by mutual agreement. We convert to successive 12-month renewals declinable on 30 days' notice, with a 60-day reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: renewal only by mutual written agreement. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | We are locked into a 36-month Initial Period with no convenience right; all termination triggers run in Licensor's favour. We add a 30-day Licensee convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination charge or acceleration of Supplemental Payments, and confirm Licensor has no convenience right during the term. |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Grant is expressly non-exclusive and nothing requires us to source solely from Licensor. The Article XXII right of first refusal is a change-of-control right, not exclusive dealing. No redline. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Fees are usage-based plus a monthly support fee, with no minimum spend, shortfall charge, acceleration or exit payment; Article XXIII bars termination damages. The audit cost-shift is reimbursement of actual cost. No redline. |
| 10 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement: | Article X contains only nondisclosure and employee non-solicitation; the Field of Use and Article II restrictions are licence-scope limits, not restraints on our business. The competitor element of the change-of-control consent is addressed under ASSIGN. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | 50+ US$5.00 | Article IV(b) permits Licensor-initiated audits with no frequency cap, no advance notice (the 30 days is our deadline to submit), no business-hours limit and no auditor confidentiality. Cost allocation and auditor selection are acceptable, so we add only frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality and no-system-access limits. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | 50+ US$5.00 | Platform fees are usage-based with no volume floor, but the USD 2,500 monthly support fee is mandatory and non-reducible for the full 36 months (~USD 90,000) with no exit. We make the support services cancellable or reducible on 30 days' notice with pro-rated fees and confirm no minimum purchase commitment. Fallback: commitment limited to 12 months with a true-up. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Article X(b) is one-way against us, runs three years post-termination and covers all Licensor and Affiliate personnel. The existing general-advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs are acceptable, so we take the fallback: mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel directly involved in the Agreement. |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Article XXI runs entirely in Licensor's favour (five-day return and certification by us); nothing requires Licensor to return our hosted market data, order and trade records or to assist on wind-down. We insert a new Article XXI-A: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, then certified deletion. Fallback: 90 days. |
| 15 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | WARRANTY DISCLAIMER | Article VIX is a pure "AS IS" disclaimer of all express and implied warranties, including any commitment that nonconformity will be corrected. We insert a limited warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformity to Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/refund remedy, carved out of the disclaimer. Fallback: 90-day conformity period. |
| 16 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Article XXIV(a) selects New York law with exclusive venue in New York state courts and the S.D.N.Y., plus venue and forum non conveniens waivers. No arbitration provision. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | No pricing-parity or most-favoured-nation obligation runs against us; commercial terms are fixed-rate or revenue-share. The "other licensees" reference regarding Revisions operates in our favour. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | GENERAL PROVISIONS | No insurance article; the only insurance reference is a cost pass-through to us. Licensor hosts the technology through which our market data and orders are transmitted. We insert a covenant at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request). Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These findings are expressly identified as at or beyond our playbook walk-away lines and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a one-way Licensee indemnity for Licensor's technology (INDEMN)** — the combination of the absent Licensor IP indemnity, the broad Article XII obligation on us, and the Article XIII(a) disclaimer of Licensor liability for IP infringement is the express walk-away scenario.
2. **One-sided liability cap at one half of amounts paid (LOL-CAP)** — below the six-months'-fees floor, with our own liability uncapped and no Excluded Claims.
3. **Assignment and change of control (ASSIGN)** — both limbs are at or beyond the line: a blanket one-way bar on our assignment, and automatic termination on our change of control at Licensor's discretion.
4. **Unilateral seven-year renewal at Licensor's option (RENEWAL)** — an automatic multi-year renewal without our consent.
5. **Unlimited, on-demand audit rights against us (AUDIT)** — no frequency cap, notice period or auditor confidentiality.
6. **Three-year, all-personnel non-solicit binding only us (NOSOLICIT)** — both duration and scope are in the walk-away zone; we have proposed the fallback rather than deletion.
7. **Pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no performance warranty (WARRANTY)**.

Items 1–3 are critical and, in our view, non-negotiable in substance. Items 4–7 have workable fallbacks already drafted.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering all 13 deviation/missing findings; the five compliant rules require no change and should not be reopened.
2. **Sequence the negotiation** around the three critical items first — Licensor indemnity with an express carve-out from the Article XIII exclusions and cap (without it, the indemnity is nullified), the mutual cap and Excluded Claims, and the IP carve-out for Licensee Data and paid-for customization deliverables.
3. **Bundle the lock-in package** (T4C, renewal, licence scope for Affiliates/contractors, assignment and change of control, support-fee commitment) as a single commercial trade, since together they determine our ability to exit and to integrate the platform across the group.
4. **Confirm the operational items** with the business: transition assistance and data-return timing for our hosted trading records, acceptable audit notice and frequency, and whether Licensor can meet the preferred insurance limits or requires the fallback.
5. **Escalate** to the deal principal if Licensor refuses the Licensor indemnity, the mutual cap, or removal of the change-of-control termination right, given their walk-away status.
6. **Re-run this review** against Licensor's turn to confirm the Article XIII carve-outs survive and that no new definitions (in particular "Derivative Work" and "Change of Control") are re-scoped in ways that reintroduce the issues above."}

## 3. Walk-away items

These findings are expressly identified as at or beyond our playbook walk-away lines and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a one-way Licensee indemnity for Licensor's technology (INDEMN)** — the combination of the absent Licensor IP indemnity, the broad Article XII obligation on us, and the Article XIII(a) disclaimer of Licensor liability for IP infringement is the express walk-away scenario.
2. **One-sided liability cap at one half of amounts paid (LOL-CAP)** — below the six-months'-fees floor, with our own liability uncapped and no Excluded Claims.
3. **Assignment and change of control (ASSIGN)** — both limbs are at or beyond the line: a blanket one-way bar on our assignment, and automatic termination on our change of control at Licensor's discretion.
4. **Unilateral seven-year renewal at Licensor's option (RENEWAL)** — an automatic multi-year renewal without our consent.
5. **Unlimited, on-demand audit rights against us (AUDIT)** — no frequency cap, notice period or auditor confidentiality.
6. **Three-year, all-personnel non-solicit binding only us (NOSOLICIT)** — both duration and scope are in the walk-away zone; we have proposed the fallback rather than deletion.
7. **Pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no performance warranty (WARRANTY)**.

Items 1–3 are critical and, in our view, non-negotiable in substance. Items 4–7 have workable fallbacks already drafted.
